The Inspector General of Police, Olatunji Disu, has ordered the redeployment of 128 senior police officers, comprising 22 Commissioners of Police and 106 Assistant Commissioners of Police, to various departments, formations and commands across the country. The postings, contained in two police wireless messages dated November 16, 2026, affect key operational, investigative, administrative and specialised units of the Nigeria Police Force. According to one of the messages, “The IGP has ordered the posting of the following CPs as indicated against their names.” Among the Commissioners of Police affected, Arikpo Ofemi Ikpi was posted to the Special Enquiry Bureau of the Force Criminal Investigation Department Annex in Lagos, while Felix Akoneme Nnebue was deployed to the Anti-Human Trafficking unit in Abuja. Mamman Bitrus Giwa was posted to the Special Enquiry Bureau of the FCID in Abuja, while Charles E. Dike was deployed to the Special Protection Unit at the Force Headquarters. Other commissioners affected include Nelson Nwamana, posted as CP Administration, FCID Annex, Lagos; Nache Bashiru Liman, CP General Investigation, FCID Annex, Kaduna; Emman Adegboyega Oyeleye, CP Interpol, Lagos; and Isiaka Salau Oyenuga, CP Anti-Fraud, FCID Annex, Enugu. Abdulkarim Musa Waziri was posted as CP INEC, Abuja, while Mohammed Yusuf Adamu was deployed as CP Railway. Among them, Rex Abiodun Enwelike was posted to the Ozoro Divisional Training School, while Raji Ganiyu was deployed to Area Command J, Ajah, Lagos. Samuel Ijachi was posted to the 70 Police Mobile Force, Kabba, Kogi State; Mohammed Temitope Ogunrin to the 16 Police Mobile Force, Abeokuta, Ogun State; and Idris Bunu to the 75 Police Mobile Force, Obudu, Cross River State. Other ACPs were deployed to the Force Criminal Investigation Department, State Criminal Investigation Departments, X-Squad, Special Fraud Unit, railway police and various zonal commands. The wireless messages directed the relevant departments and formations to update their records accordingly. The PUNCH had on Monday reported that Disu ordered the posting of 13 Assistant Inspectors-General of Police and two Commissioners of Police to new commands and departments across the country, according to a police wireless message dated November 15.
